transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I just… I honestly don’t see things getting back on track anymore. The studio, my life, all of it. No matter how hard I work or what kind of payment plan they put in front of me, it feels like it’s not going to turn around.
Have you had thoughts of killing yourself?
I’m… not sure how to answer that. I mean, I’ve felt really hopeless, but I don’t know that I’d say I’ve been thinking of killing myself.
Did this start after a particular stressful event?

Yeah… I’d say it started around when I took on the mortgage for the studio. That was a little over two years ago now—about two years and a couple months. Since then it’s just felt like it’s been hanging over me.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?

Yeah. Most days, honestly. I wake up and it’s like there’s this heavy gray feeling already there. Even when I’m in the shop, around the wood and the work I used to care about, it just feels flat. Some days I have to push myself not to just stand there staring.
Before this started two years ago, had you ever gone through another period in your life when you felt depressed like this for at least two weeks?
I don’t really know. I mean, I’ve had rough stretches before like anyone, but I can’t remember another time where it went on like this for weeks. Nothing that stands out to me like this.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
I’m not sure. I mean… things don’t feel the same as they used to, but I don’t know if I’d call it losing interest exactly. It’s just harder to care about much.
Have you been worrying a lot?
I don’t know… not especially, I guess. I think about things, sure, but I wouldn’t say I’m worrying a lot more than usual.
Have these feelings made it hard for you to keep up with your work?

Yeah. It’s gotten pretty bad. I’ve missed bids and lost clients who used to call me first. Even the basic stuff, like keeping up with paperwork for the mortgage, just piles up because I can’t seem to stay on top of it.

I’ve also stopped going to gallery openings and playing pickup basketball, so it’s not just the work. I’m barely hanging onto the things and people that used to be part of my life.
Have you been feeling worthless or like you’ve let people down?

Yeah… I do. When something goes wrong, I don’t just see it as one mistake. Like if a joint doesn’t line up right, or I miss a bid deadline, I start thinking I’m just a lousy carpenter. Like maybe I had no business trying to run my own studio in the first place.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I lose track of things sometimes, but I don’t know if that’s concentration exactly. I haven’t been paying close attention to it.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?
I’m not really sure. My sleep hasn’t been something I’ve been tracking closely. Some nights feel rough, but I can’t say for sure if it’s a real pattern.
Have you noticed a change in your appetite?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed a clear change one way or the other. Some days I don’t think much about eating, but I couldn’t say it’s been different in a definite way.
If the mortgage situation were resolved, do you think you’d still feel this depressed?

Honestly, I think I would. The mortgage makes it worse, sure, but most days I wake up already feeling this heavy, gray feeling. Even when I’m in the shop around wood and tools—stuff I used to really care about—it just feels flat. I have to push myself not to just stand there staring.
Have you been moving or speaking more slowly than usual?

I don’t really know. I haven’t noticed myself talking slower, but I guess I’m not always paying attention to that. Moving around… maybe I feel sluggish sometimes, but I couldn’t say if it looks slower to other people.
Have you been wishing you wouldn’t wake up or that you could just disappear?
I… I don’t know. I haven’t really thought about it in those words. I don’t think I can give you a clear answer on that right now.
Have you been wishing you were dead?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I can say it that clearly. It’s… hard to sort out what I’m feeling right now.
Have you been thinking that you would be better off dead?
I don’t know. I’ve had some pretty dark thoughts, but saying I’d be better off dead… I’m not sure I can put it that way.
Have you been feeling tired or low on energy nearly every day?

Yeah. Pretty much every day. Even if I’ve been in bed all night, by midmorning my arms feel like I’ve already been hauling lumber all day. I can still do things, but measuring, cutting, returning calls… it all takes more out of me than it should. I feel wiped out.
During these past two years, have you felt depressed or down most of the day more days than not?

Yeah. Most days, I wake up and it’s already there, this heavy gray feeling. It sticks around a lot of the day. Even when I’m in the shop around the wood and tools, the stuff I used to care about, it just feels flat, and I have to push myself not to just stand there staring.
During the past two years, was there ever a stretch of more than two months when you did not feel depressed?

No, not really. It’s been pretty steady since I took on the mortgage for the studio… a little over two years ago. So, about two years and two months now. I can’t think of a stretch longer than a couple months where it wasn’t there.
